requirements.quote: The value of Will QoS is 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02).
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating the Will QoS field in a CONNECT message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use only Will QoS value 0, 1, or 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept any other Will QoS value.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Will QoS value can be inspected and compared with the finite allowed set.

requirements.quote: Bits 7, 6, and 0 of this byte are not used in the current version of the protocol. They are reserved for future use.
requirements.condition: When processing the Connect flags byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat bits 7, 6, and 0 as reserved and without current protocol semantics.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use bits 7, 6, or 0 for current-version protocol behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's encoder, decoder, and flag handling can be checked for any assigned semantics or use of these bit positions.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 5 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the Will Retain flag.
requirements.required_behavior: Place and read the Will Retain flag at bit 5 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or interpret the Will Retain flag at another bit position.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag's position can be verified directly from serialized CONNECT packets.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag indicates whether or not broker should retain the Will message which is published by the broker on behalf of the client in the event that the client is disconnected unexpectedly.
requirements.condition: When a client is disconnected unexpectedly and the broker publishes its Will message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will Retain flag to determine whether the broker retains the published Will message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make Will-message retention behavior inconsistent with the Will Retain flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker can be exercised with each flag value followed by an unexpected disconnect, and retained-message state can be observed.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag is mandatory if the Will flag is set, otherwise, it is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Supply and process the Will Retain flag.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT parsing and subsequent Will handling can verify that the flag is processed whenever the Will flag is set.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag is mandatory if the Will flag is set, otherwise, it is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is not set.
requirements.required_behavior: Disregard the Will Retain flag.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let the Will Retain bit affect protocol behavior when the Will flag is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT packets with the Will flag clear and varying Will Retain bits can be compared for identical behavior.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive timer is present in the variable header of a MQTT CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding an MQTT CONNECT message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and parse the Keep Alive timer in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the Keep Alive timer from the CONNECT variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT variable header can be parsed to verify field presence and location.

requirements.quote: The client has a responsibility to send a message within each Keep Alive time period.
requirements.condition: For each nonzero negotiated Keep Alive time period while the connection is active.
requirements.required_behavior: The client sends a message within the Keep Alive period.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not remain silent for an entire nonzero Keep Alive period.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed client trace can establish whether at least one message is sent within every applicable interval.

requirements.quote: In the absence of a data-related message during the time period, the client sends a PINGREQ message, which the broker acknowledges with a PINGRESP message.
requirements.condition: When the client has no data-related message to send during a Keep Alive period.
requirements.required_behavior: The client sends PINGREQ, and the broker acknowledges it with PINGRESP.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client must not let the period expire without sending PINGREQ when no data-related message was sent; the broker must not leave the PINGREQ unacknowledged.
requirements.why_checkable: A timed exchange with no application data can verify both PINGREQ emission and the corresponding PINGRESP.

requirements.quote: If the broker does not receive a message from the client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period (the client is allowed "grace" of half a time period), it disconnects the client as if the client had sent a DISCONNECT message.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives no client message within 1.5 times the Keep Alive period.
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the client and apply the behavior used when the client sends DISCONNECT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not keep the client connected beyond the specified inactivity threshold.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the inactivity timeout as if a DISCONNECT message had been received.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker can be tested with a silent client and the disconnect timing and cleanup path observed.

requirements.quote: This action does not impact any of the client's subscriptions.
requirements.condition: When the broker disconnects a client because the 1.5-times-Keep-Alive inactivity limit was exceeded.
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve the client's subscriptions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not remove or alter subscriptions merely because of this timeout disconnection.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscription state can be recorded before the timeout and compared afterward.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive timer is a 16-bit value that represents the number of seconds for the time period.
requirements.condition: When encoding, decoding, or applying the Keep Alive timer.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as a 16-bit value whose unit is seconds.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode it at another width or interpret it using another time unit.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized width and timeout calculations can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: A value of zero (0) means the client is not disconnected.
requirements.condition: When the Keep Alive timer value is zero.
requirements.required_behavior: Do not disconnect the client because of Keep Alive inactivity.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply the Keep Alive inactivity-disconnect timer.
requirements.why_checkable: A silent connection using zero Keep Alive can be observed beyond ordinary Keep Alive thresholds.

requirements.quote: The ordering of the 2 bytes of the Keep Alive Timer is MSB, then LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing the two-byte Keep Alive timer.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode the most significant byte first and the least significant byte second.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use little-endian byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: The byte sequence for a non-symmetric test value directly reveals byte order.

requirements.quote: The connect return code is resent in the variable header of a MQTT CONNACK message.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding an MQTT CONNACK message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and parse the connect return code in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or place the connect return code outside the CONNACK variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized CONNACK can be parsed to verify the field's presence and location.

requirements.quote: This field defines a one byte unsigned return code.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the connect return code.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the return code as a one-byte unsigned value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode it using a signed interpretation or a width other than one byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized width and numeric interpretation can be tested for boundary values.

requirements.quote: 0	0x00	Connection Accepted
requirements.condition: When the connect return code is 0x00.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret and emit it as Connection Accepted.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not treat 0x00 as a connection refusal.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNACK with code 0x00 can be checked against the connection state selected by the implementation.

requirements.quote: 1	0x01	Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version
requirements.condition: When refusing a connection because the protocol version is unacceptable.
requirements.required_behavior: Use return code 0x01 and interpret 0x01 as that refusal reason.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret 0x01 as acceptance or another defined refusal reason.
requirements.error_behavior: Report Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted or parsed byte and resulting refusal reason can be compared with 0x01.

requirements.quote: 2	0x02	Connection Refused: identifier rejected
requirements.condition: When refusing a connection because the identifier is rejected.
requirements.required_behavior: Use return code 0x02 and interpret 0x02 as that refusal reason.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret 0x02 as acceptance or another defined refusal reason.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted or parsed byte and resulting refusal reason can be compared with 0x02.

requirements.quote: 3	0x03	Connection Refused: broker unavailable
requirements.condition: When refusing a connection because the broker is unavailable.
requirements.required_behavior: Use return code 0x03 and interpret 0x03 as that refusal reason.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret 0x03 as acceptance or another defined refusal reason.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted or parsed byte and resulting refusal reason can be compared with 0x03.

requirements.quote: 4-255	Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: When emitting or interpreting a current-version connect return code.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat values 4 through 255 as reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign current-version connect-result semantics to values 4 through 255.
requirements.why_checkable: Defined code tables and runtime handling can be checked for assignments in the reserved range.

requirements.quote: The topic name is present in the variable header of an MQTT PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding an MQTT PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and parse the topic name in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the topic name or place it outside the PUBLISH variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized PUBLISH variable header can be inspected for the field.

requirements.quote: The topic name is a UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a PUBLISH topic name.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and parse the topic name as a UTF-encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an incompatible string encoding.
requirements.why_checkable: The topic field's bytes can be validated against the specified UTF string format in this chunk.

requirements.quote: Topic name has an upper length limit of 32,767 characters.
requirements.condition: When accepting or producing a topic name.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the topic name to at most 32,767 characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or emit a topic name longer than 32,767 characters.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests at 32,767 and 32,768 characters can verify enforcement.

requirements.quote: The payload part of a PUBLISH message contains application-specific data only.
requirements.condition: When constructing or interpreting a PUBLISH payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the payload contents as application-specific data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place MQTT protocol header fields in the PUBLISH payload.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload construction and parsing can be inspected for protocol-level fields or assumptions.

requirements.quote: No assumptions are made about the nature or content of the data, and this part of the message is treated as a BLOB.
requirements.condition: When an MQTT implementation handles a PUBLISH payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the payload as an opaque BLOB without imposing content semantics.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require a particular application-data type or content structure at the MQTT layer.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply arbitrary binary payloads and verify transparent transport without MQTT-layer reinterpretation.

requirements.quote: If you want an application to apply compression to the payload data, you need to define in the application the appropriate payload flag fields to handle the compression details.
requirements.condition: When an application applies compression to MQTT payload data.
requirements.required_behavior: Define and handle compression indicators as part of the application payload protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be inspected to verify that compression metadata belongs to the application-defined payload format.

requirements.quote: You cannot define application-specific flags in the fixed or variable headers.
requirements.condition: When extending an application carried over MQTT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not define or encode application-specific flags in MQTT fixed or variable headers.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet layouts and extension code can be inspected for application-defined header bits or fields.

requirements.quote: The message identifier is present in the variable header of the following MQTT messages: PUBLISH, PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: When determining which MQTT message types may carry a Message Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the Message Identifier in the variable header of applicable PUBLISH, PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, and UNSUBACK messages.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place a Message Identifier in an MQTT message type outside this enumerated set.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoders and decoders can be tested across all MQTT message types for field presence and location.

requirements.quote: The Message Identifier (Message ID) field is only present in messages where the QoS bits in the fixed header indicate QoS levels 1 or 2.
requirements.condition: When the fixed-header QoS bits do not indicate QoS level 1 or 2.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit the Message ID field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include a Message ID when the QoS bits indicate another level.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets at each QoS value can be parsed to verify conditional field absence.

requirements.quote: The Message Identifier (Message ID) field is only present in messages where the QoS bits in the fixed header indicate QoS levels 1 or 2.
requirements.condition: When a Message ID field is present.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the fixed-header QoS bits indicate QoS level 1 or 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept Message ID presence with QoS bits outside levels 1 and 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The relationship between a parsed Message ID and the packet's QoS bits can be checked mechanically.

requirements.quote: The Message ID is a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.condition: When encoding, decoding, or storing an MQTT Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Message ID as a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode it at another width or interpret it as signed.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized width and numeric boundary behavior can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: This assumes that there are never more than 65,535 messages "in flight" between one particular client-broker pair at any time.
requirements.condition: For any particular client-broker pair.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit simultaneously in-flight messages to no more than 65,535.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not allow more than 65,535 messages to remain in flight for the pair at one time.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's in-flight tracking can be stress-tested and counted at the boundary.

requirements.quote: The ordering of the two bytes of the Message Identifier is MSB, then LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing a Message Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and decode the most significant byte first and the least significant byte second.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use little-endian byte order.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-symmetric Message ID value directly reveals the byte order on the wire.

requirements.quote: Do not use Message ID 0. It is reserved as an invalid Message ID.
requirements.condition: When allocating, emitting, receiving, or validating a Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat zero as an invalid and reserved Message ID.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use Message ID 0.
requirements.error_behavior: Reject or otherwise handle Message ID 0 as invalid.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets and allocator output can be tested explicitly with identifier zero.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol uses a subset of UTF-8. Only single byte (non-extended) characters are supported.
requirements.condition: When encoding or validating an MQTT UTF string.
requirements.required_behavior: Support only single-byte, non-extended characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not emit or accept multibyte or extended UTF-8 characters.
requirements.why_checkable: Strings containing single-byte and multibyte UTF-8 sequences can be tested at the encoder and decoder.

requirements.quote:
byte 1	Message Length MSB

byte 2	Message Length LSB

bytes 3 ...	Encoded Character Data
requirements.condition: When serializing or parsing an MQTT UTF string.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode byte 1 as the message-length MSB, byte 2 as the message-length LSB, and subsequent bytes as encoded character data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reverse the length bytes or place character data before the two-byte length prefix.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized string can be inspected byte-by-byte for prefix order and data placement.

requirements.quote: Message Length is the number of bytes of encoded string characters, not the number of characters.
requirements.condition: When calculating or validating the length prefix of an MQTT UTF string.
requirements.required_behavior: Set and interpret Message Length as the byte count of the encoded character data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not calculate the field as a character count when that differs from the encoded-byte count.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared length can be compared mechanically with the number of following encoded-character bytes.

requirements.quote: For ASCII strings, however, these are the same.
requirements.condition: When the MQTT UTF string contains only supported single-byte ASCII characters.
requirements.required_behavior: The encoded-byte length and character count are equal.
requirements.why_checkable: Both counts can be calculated from any encoded ASCII test string and compared.

requirements.quote:
The format of encoded characters for ASCII codes 0x01 to 0x7F are shown in the table below.

bit	7	6	5	4	3	2	1	0

0	ASCII code of character
requirements.condition: When encoding an ASCII character with code 0x01 through 0x7F in an MQTT UTF string.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as one byte with bit 7 equal to zero and bits 6 through 0 containing the ASCII character code.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an extended or multibyte representation for these characters.
requirements.why_checkable: Each permitted ASCII code has a deterministic one-byte representation whose high bit and lower seven bits can be inspected.
